 BMW recalls over 720,000 vehicles after unresolved defect poses fire risk
 Owners should keep those vehicles away from garages, carports, and other vehicles.
 by James Nanzo November 20, 2026 
 share
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Link Copied! 
 Photo Credit: iStock
 An unsuccessful earlier repair has prompted BMW to recall 720,796 vehicles in the U.S. The unresolved defect poses a fire risk even when a vehicle is parked and turned off.
 Here's what to know
 As Motor1 detailed, older 3 Series and 5 Series cars, multiple 2 Series and 4 Series body styles, and the Z4, X1, X3, X4, and X5 are among the affected vehicles. The recall spans model years 2012–2018.
 BMW submitted recall 26V733000 to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) on November 4, 2026.
 Water reaching the water pump's electrical terminals can trigger a short circuit and fire, BMW said in the recall document . A seal protects that electrical connection, but it can fail and let water through.
 More background
 According to Motor1, owners whose vehicles received a connector repair under campaign 24V608 still face a short-circuit risk. The new recall replaces that unsuccessful effort to correct the same connector problem.
 Further testing revealed brittle, cracked material in the connector, BMW reported in its Part 573 filing for the replacement recall.

 Motor1 also reported that BMW's September 2026 park-outside warning concerned a starter relay defect affecting 3, 5, and 7 Series sedans. The automaker had issued a separate park-outside warning in August 2026.
 The recall document also estimated that the defect impacts fewer than  0.1% of vehicles. That is of little solace to the unlucky owners who experience issues. 
 The recall document said BMW is aware of around 10 field instances where the defect came into play. It said it had not received reports, nor was it aware of any accidents or injuries connected to the defect.
 What can be done?
 Motor1 noted affected vehicles will receive a free dealership repair, even if they were serviced under the earlier recall. If drivers paid for repairs in the past, they might be eligible for reimbursement. 
 BMW is still developing the remedy, however, and dealers cannot book appointments until it is finalized and parts are available.
 NHTSA's instruction to park outdoors applies even when an affected vehicle shows no obvious signs of a connector problem. While awaiting a repair, owners should keep those vehicles away from garages, carports, and other vehicles.
 Owners can arrange dealership service once a second letter announces that the repair is available. The first notice, scheduled for December 2026, will confirm whether their vehicle is covered by the recall.
 Owners with questions can contact BMW customer service at 1-800-525-7417. Vehicle identification numbers associated with recall 26V733000 are scheduled to be available for lookup on NHTSA.gov beginning December 25, 2026, per the recall report .
